events.label: Ordinance of the Jewry
events.detail: Deeds of Jewish lenders to be executed before appointed Christian and Jewish clerks in six or seven towns, one part kept in a public chest (archa).

events.label: Domus Conversorum founded
events.detail: Henry III orders a house for converted Jews on what is now Chancery Lane, endowed at 700 marks a year.

events.label: Statute of the Jewry
events.detail: Edward I forbids Jewish moneylending and allows Jews to trade or live by their labour.

events.label: Coinage arrests
events.detail: All the Jews of England imprisoned in one night, their property seized and houses searched, ahead of an inquiry into the coinage.
events.ref: Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. VIII, c. p. 49

events.label: Inquiry into the Domus
events.detail: An inquiry covering 1280 to 1308 lists 34 converts alive in 1280 and since dead, and 23 men and 28 women living.
events.ref: Adler, Domus Conversorum, App. III, pp. 38–39

events.label: Order to remove Jews from towns without chests
events.detail: Draft order to the justices of the Jews that Jews be peaceably removed from cities and towns where there are no archae.

events.label: Expulsion from Gascony
events.detail: Edward I, in Gascony, orders all Jews to leave the duchy.
events.ref: Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. XI (the OCR text gives no year; 1287 is reference knowledge)

events.label: Chevage for the converts
events.detail: Two converts commissioned to collect the poll tax on Jews of twelve and over for the Domus.

events.label: Writs of expulsion
events.detail: Writs to the sheriffs: all Jews to leave England before All Saints (1 November), on pain of death.
events.ref: Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. XI, c. p. 69

events.label: Safe-conduct to the Cinque Ports
events.detail: The ports to give the departing Jews, their wives, children and goods safe and speedy passage at moderate charges.

events.label: The Jews of York
events.detail: Safe-conducts for Bonamy of York, his son Jocem and the other Jews of York.

events.label: The London Jews leave
events.detail: On St Denis’s Day the Jews of London set out for the coast. A shipmaster drowns a party of the richer exiles at the mouth of the Thames; he and his accomplices are later hanged.
events.ref: Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. XI, c. pp. 70–71

events.label: New keeper of the Domus
events.detail: Walter de Agmodesham appointed keeper of the Domus Conversorum.

events.label: All Saints: the deadline
events.detail: The term set by the writs of 18 July. One party of 1,335, mostly poor, went to Flanders; others reached France, where in 1291 they were ordered to leave.
events.ref: Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. XI, c. p. 71

events.label: Eighty converts
events.detail: Eighty converted Jews were receiving the king’s alms in the year of the Expulsion: 1½d. a day for a man, 1d. for a woman.
events.ref: Adler, Domus Conversorum, pp. 2–3 (Patent Roll 1290, m. 19)

events.label: Sale of the houses
events.detail: Hugh de Kendale appointed to value and sell the houses, rents and tenements of the Jews. Abrahams: their yearly value was about £130; nearly all were given to the king’s friends.
events.ref: CPR 1281–92, p. 410; Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. XI, c. pp. 72–73

events.label: Chests delivered to the Exchequer
events.detail: Memorandum of the delivery of the chests of chirographs of Jews to the treasurer and barons. Abrahams puts the registered debts at about £9,100.
events.ref: TNA E 101/249/29; Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. XI, c. p. 72

events.label: Northampton: the School of the Jews
events.detail: Edward I grants the School of the Jews of Northampton to St James’s Abbey.

events.label: Hereford houses granted
events.detail: Houses of Civitasse, Elias de Ardre and Aaron le Blund, Jews of Hereford, granted at nominal rents.

events.label: The converts’ endowment
events.detail: £202 0s. 4d. a year at the Exchequer for the converts, each portion to lapse at the convert’s death.

events.label: Colchester: the School of the Jews
events.detail: The School of the Jews and eight Jewish households’ houses at Colchester granted to William son of Jordan de Brokesburn.

events.label: The London synagogue
events.detail: The chapel of the Friars of the Sack in Coleman Street, ‘lately the synagogue of the Jews’, assigned for a chantry.

events.label: Debts still outstanding
events.detail: Confirmations of 1315 and 1327 of the renunciation of interest show debts to the Jews still being collected; Edward III gave up the claim.
events.ref: Abrahams, Expulsion (1895), ch. XI, c. p. 73

events.label: ‘About ninety years’
events.detail: A York title case in King’s Bench pleads back to the time when ‘the Jews were put into exile out of the realm of England, about ninety years since’ (circiter quaterviginti et decem annos elapsos).
events.ref: Glyph Machina, KB27 roll 432, fronts, image 0175, and dorses, image 0341 (dated 1354 and c. 1367 by Glyph Machina)

events.label: The Domus annexed to the Rolls
events.detail: The Domus Conversorum annexed for ever to the office of Keeper of the Rolls of Chancery.

events.label: Elizabeth, daughter of Rabbi Moses
events.detail: A convert in the Domus, daughter of ‘the bishop of the Jews’, given an extra penny a day.

events.label: Lincoln: the last small sums
events.detail: Small yearly sums from Lincoln houses late of Ursel Levy, Diabella and Belasset granted away by the Crown.

events.label: Last escheat charge found
events.detail: The Lincoln charge on the houses of Diabella, held by the heirs of Robert de Leverton, still on the pipe roll.
events.ref: Glyph Machina, E372 roll 405, fronts, image 0032

events.label: Last resident in Adler’s list
events.detail: Nathaniel Menda, formerly Jehooda Menda, in the Domus 1578–1608; Adler counts 48 inmates from 1330 to 1608.

events.label: Readmission
events.detail: Adler’s ‘Middle Period’ of Anglo-Jewish history closes with Cromwell; the date of readmission is reference knowledge.

props.origin_note: The entries cite the pipe rolls of 16 and 27 Henry III (1231–32, 1242–43): the charge predates 1290.

flags.title: The formula is not proof of an Expulsion escheat
flags.text: The phrase “que fuerunt … Iudei” marks a Jewish former owner. The two Bristol charges that run longest (to 1529 and 1575) cite pipe rolls of 16 and 27 Henry III and a grant of 1241; Diabella of Lincoln is “dampnata” and Vives le Yonge of Oxford “suspensus”. Only some of the long charges began in 1290. The Houses & rents view sorts each charge by what its own entries say.

flags.title: Wickford is Wigford
flags.text: The earlier sweep placed a Jewish escheat at Wickford (E368 roll 239, image 0084). The entries name Ursel Levy “de Wikeford in parochia Sancti Marci”, and CPR 1461–67, p. 499 puts his houses in Lincoln: Wigford, the suburb with St Mark’s church.

flags.title: The 1559 roll
flags.text: The sweep called E372 roll 401 (image 0032) “Marian” and grouped it with the Bristol charge. The hit read here is dated 1559 (Elizabeth I) and charges Lincoln houses of Diabella and Belasset.

flags.title: Raw counts after 1290 are mostly noise
flags.text: An any-word search for iudeus, iudei, iudeorum and five other forms returns 37,683 entries, more after 1290 than before. In a sample of 25 Common Pleas hits from the 1330s, the matches are “Iudeo” for ideo (“Ideo sicut pluries preceptum est”) and the feast of SS Simon and Jude (“festum apostolorum Simonis et Iude”); none clearly names a Jew. The Overview uses anchored formulae only; the raw curve is shown in Sources & method as a warning.

flags.title: Two keepers in 1327
flags.text: The Patent Roll grants the Domus to Richard de Ayremynne for life in March 1327, but a 1341 exemplification recites letters of 7 November, 1 Edward III, appointing Adam de Osgodeby. One reading is wrong, or the grants overlap.

flags.title: Walter of Nottingham
flags.text: Adler’s first post-Expulsion inmate is “Walter of Nottingham” (1330–36). The Patent Roll protection of March 1331 names “Master Walter de Croydon … lately received among the conversi”, dated at Nottingham. Adler may have taken the place-date for a surname, or worked from a different record.

flags.title: Exonie is Oxonie
flags.text: The HTR often reads the Oxford rents as “ville Exonie”. The house of Vives le Yonge, hanged, at first looked like an Exeter charge; other lines on the same images read “in suburbia Oxon”, and a petition of 1337–38 (SC 8/67/3303) places the toft of “Vive le Longe … hanged for felony” in the suburb of Oxford. It is mapped at Oxford.

flags.title: Chellesworthy
flags.text: The CPR’s “Chellesworthy alias Chollesworthy, co. Devon”, in the king’s hands “by the exile of the Jews” from 1401 to 1461, is mapped at Chilsworthy near Holsworthy. The identification is a guess.

flags.title: County rolls placed at towns
flags.text: The rolls of obligations of 1291–93 (E 101/250/2–12) are by county. They are placed at each county’s main Jewry (Gloucestershire at Gloucester, Wiltshire at Devizes, Huntingdon and Cambridge at Cambridge), which may not be where the chest was kept.

flags.title: Gascony, 1287
flags.text: The year of the Gascon expulsion is reference knowledge: the OCR of Abrahams has no year at that point and misprints Edward’s departure as 1280.
